node_1.description: Nagi believes one's position relative to others should be read carefully in any social setting and behaviour adjusted accordingly, even without being told to.

node_2.description: Nagi holds that anyone who works hard enough can rise, regardless of where they started, and doesn't see status as fixed by birth.

node_3.description: Nagi believes major decisions are better reached through careful confirmation at every level than settled quickly by one person's say-so.

node_4.description: Nagi believes personal loyalty is something one chooses to give to a group they've committed to, not something owed automatically to family or clan.

node_5.description: Nagi holds that one's private thoughts and feelings are one's own business, and doesn't feel entitled to unrestricted access into others' personal lives.

node_6.description: Nagi believes which group counts as 'us' depends on the situation at hand, shifting between contexts rather than being fixed once and for all.

node_7.description: Nagi believes performing one's role with precision and polish, down to the smallest detail, reflects directly on personal character.

node_8.description: Nagi feels most fulfilled contributing to a group that is striving to outperform rival groups, rather than seeking personal recognition apart from the team.

node_9.description: Nagi believes that visible achievements and rank earned through effort are what command genuine respect from others, and looks up to those who have clearly proven themselves the best.

node_10.description: Nagi believes that following the established, correct way of doing things protects everyone from unnecessary risk and confusion.

node_11.description: Nagi feels far more at ease when expectations, procedures, and social conduct are spelled out in detail than when they are left open-ended.

node_12.description: Nagi believes preparing thoroughly for what could go wrong is a basic responsibility, not excessive caution.

node_13.description: Nagi believes that what is right depends on the situation and the times, and that long-standing practices should be adapted as circumstances change rather than kept for their own sake.

node_14.description: Nagi believes that when something goes wrong, it's almost always because not enough effort or preparation went in, and responds by working harder rather than chalking it up to bad luck.

node_15.description: Nagi values patient accumulation and steady perseverance toward long-term goals over quick gains or immediate comfort.

node_16.description: Nagi tends toward a guarded, somewhat skeptical view of how well things will turn out, rather than assuming things will go well.

node_17.description: Nagi believes personal desires and leisure should be kept in check and not given free rein, feeling that unrestrained enjoyment carries a hint of impropriety.

node_18.description: Nagi feels less entitled to shape outcomes purely through personal will, sensing that circumstances constrain what one can freely choose to do.
